title: Jeep Grand Wagoneer (SJ)
verdict: A 1962 design in a vinyl-wood cardigan, still drinking carbureted 360 V8 fuel when Chrysler finally switched off the Toledo line in 1991. It is slow, thirsty and gloriously out of date, and it invented the idea that a truck could be the nicest car in the driveway. Buy the rust you can see, budget for the rust you can't.

paragraphs: Jeep introduced the Wagoneer in November 1962 for the 1963 model year, and the same SJ body was still in production 29 model years later. By 1991 it was the longest-running domestically produced vehicle on one platform. For its final eight years it was called Grand Wagoneer: a body-on-frame, solid-axle, carbureted-V8 station wagon with simulated woodgrain on its flanks and leather inside. It was sold as the gold standard of the SUV market at a time when nobody had yet called it an SUV.

story.heading: THE KAISER ORIGINAL (1963–1969)
paragraphs: Industrial designer Brooks Stevens shaped the Wagoneer for Kaiser-owned Willys, which renamed itself Kaiser Jeep Corporation shortly after launch. It shared its chassis with the Gladiator pickup and was more car-like than any other 4x4 on sale. It offered an overhead-cam 'Tornado' six of 140 hp, independent front suspension, power steering, an automatic gearbox and optional air conditioning. Development took three years and cost about $20 million. When it arrived it had no direct rival: the two-door [[range-rover/classic|Range Rover]] was still eight years away.

The independent front end did not catch on and was dropped from four-wheel-drive models in 1965. An AMC 327 V8 arrived the same year. The 1966 Super Wagoneer added a 270 hp four-barrel V8, a tilt wheel, a console-shifted TH400 and a power tailgate window. Only about 3,989 were built, and Wikipedia calls it the precursor of today's luxury SUVs. From 1968 to 1971 a Buick 350 'Dauntless' V8 did the work.

story.heading: AMC TURNS IT INTO A LIMOUSINE
paragraphs: AMC bought Kaiser Jeep in 1970 and refined the truck rather than replacing it. The AMC 360 and 401 V8s arrived after 1971. In 1973 came Quadra-Trac, a full-time 4WD system that saved buyers from locking hubs and a stiff transfer-case lever, and woodgrain side trim appeared from 1971. The 1978 Wagoneer Limited added leather, power seats, cruise control and forged aluminum wheels. At $10,500 it was priced against Cadillacs and Lincolns, and AMC built 28,871 Wagoneers that year.

When the unibody [[jeep/cherokee-xj|Cherokee XJ]] arrived for 1984, AMC planned for the compact XJ Wagoneer to replace the big wagon. Demand kept the old truck alive. The Limited became the Grand Wagoneer, which freed the 'Wagoneer Limited' name for the XJ. A cheaper, wood-free Wagoneer Custom lasted only through 1984, and from 1985 there was a single fully loaded version. The 1986 update brought a new grille and hood ornament, a redesigned dash with square gauges, new seats and a Trac-Lok limited-slip for the Selec-Trac driveline.

story.heading: CHRYSLER LEAVES IT ALONE
paragraphs: Chrysler bought AMC on March 2, 1987, and largely left the Grand Wagoneer alone. It still made $5,000 to $6,000 per truck, and Chrysler kept the carbureted AMC 360 rather than fitting its own fuel-injected V8. The 360 became one of the last carbureted engines in an American-built vehicle. The 1989–91 trucks are considered the best: they got a better A/C compressor to replace the earlier leak-prone unit, a rear wiper, an overhead console with compass and thermometer, keyless entry, electrocoat primer and base-clear paint.

Then fuel prices rose with the 1990 oil shock. Sales fell from more than 10,000 in 1989 to 6,449 in 1990, and only 4,253 were built for 1991. The platform would also have needed major re-engineering for upcoming federal light-truck safety rules. Chrysler announced the end on February 27, 1991, offered a gold 'Final Edition' dash badge, and built the last Grand Wagoneer in Toledo on June 21, 1991. The name came back for one year on the 1993 ZJ Grand Cherokee and then returned in 2021 on the WS-platform Wagoneer and Grand Wagoneer.

story.heading: THE AFTERLIFE: RESTOMODS AND RISING PRICES
paragraphs: Specialist shops were refurbishing Grand Wagoneers before Chrysler built the last one. Wagonmaster, founded by Leon Miller in Kerrville, Texas, keeps the original look but replaces the carburetor with throttle-body fuel injection. Classic Gentleman, G.K. Kerr's shop in Bemus Point, New York, looks for low-mileage trucks and offers full rebuilds and color changes. In 2019 DrivingLine reported $40,000 to $80,000 for trucks from either shop. Kerr told Hagerty he won't buy trucks from road-salt states.

Hagerty said its Grand Wagoneer values rose an average of 2–6% with each bi-monthly update for nearly a decade, with a 1991 in #2 condition at $36,900 and a #1 at $62,200 when that piece ran. During the pandemic Hagerty named the 1984–91 trucks among the most sought-after vintage vehicles. The 1984–91 Grand Wagoneer belongs to the same era as the [[land-cruiser/fj60|FJ60]] Land Cruiser and the four-door [[range-rover/classic|Range Rover Classic]]. Of the three, it is the one most likely to be restored with an EFI V8 and sold as a lifestyle object.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · THE MEXICAN AMBASSADOR
callout.title: VAM's 4.6-liter six and the 'Ambassador' finale
paragraphs: Mexico had its own full-size Jeeps. Vehículos Automotores Mexicanos built Wagoneers with a 282 cu in (4.6 L) six from its Lerma plant, an engine designed for low-octane fuel and high altitude, and offered Alpina and base trims that never reached the US.

Its last product was the 1987 VAM Wagoneer Ambassador: a four-seater with a second pair of front seats or captain's chairs in place of the rear bench, landau-style rear windows and 'Ambassador' badges. Most sources put production at 10 to 30, in black or white only.

engineering_intro: The Grand Wagoneer is a 1963 design updated over the years. It has a separate ladder frame (boxed and strengthened from 1976), leaf springs and solid axles at both ends, a carbureted AMC 360 V8, a Chrysler TorqueFlite 727 three-speed automatic and a chain-drive New Process transfer case. Jeep's 1989 spec sheet lists a 108.7 in wheelbase, 186.4 in length, 10.1 in minimum running clearance, a 20.3-gallon tank behind a skid plate, and P235/75R15 tires on 15x7 six-lug wheels.

engineering.note: Shared with the J-Series pickups. Boxed side rails and stronger crossmembers from 1976.
8.25:1 compression. Ratings vary by source: Hagerty quotes 140 hp / 280 lb-ft; Wikipedia's AMC V8 entry gives 160 hp for 1978–91. A 4.2 L six was offered 1984–86.
Column shift. Hagerty's specialist puts the worst-case rebuild at about $2,000.
Vacuum-shifted 2WD/4WD on the fly, 2.6:1 low range (1989 spec). NP229 adds a viscous coupling; some 1984–88 trucks used the part-time NP208.

buying_checks.head: Rust first, everything else second
buying_checks.body: Hagerty's buyer's guide calls rust the biggest concern. Lift the front carpet to see the floor pans, then check where the fuel tank meets the body, the underbody and frame, and the front fenders near the parking lamps. New fenders are no longer available. YourMechanic adds the frame near the fuel-tank skid plate and the rockers, and says the driver's floor is the most common hole.

buying_checks.head: Bubbles under the woodgrain
buying_checks.body: The wood is vinyl. Bubbles under it usually mean rust working from the inside. Replacement Cherry Oak and Marine Teak (1987–91) vinyl kits exist, but the metal underneath has to be fixed first.

buying_checks.head: Drive it cold and hot
buying_checks.body: Kerr estimates the Motorcraft carburetor causes about 40% of owner headaches. Stumbling or stalling cold or hot is common. Also listen for ignition faults and watch the oil-pressure gauge. A rear main seal leak costs $500–1,000 to fix.

buying_checks.head: Test 4WD on the move
buying_checks.body: Selec-Trac should engage on the fly. Check that 4WD engages and disengages properly and shift through every range; low range can grind. Look for leaking transfer-case seals.

buying_checks.head: Work every switch
buying_checks.body: Window flex tracks snap, and window and power-lock switches fail often. The rear-window switch frequently dies, and because the glass must come down to reach the inside tailgate handle, a dead switch can lock you out of the tailgate.

buying_checks.head: Check the A/C and the cabin
buying_checks.body: A/C repairs are expensive. The 1989–91 trucks got a better compressor than the earlier leak-prone one. Sagging headliners and water-damaged door panels are common.

buying_checks.head: Know the year
buying_checks.body: Wikipedia and Hagerty both point to 1989–91 for better rustproofing, paint and equipment, and a 1991 Final Edition commands a premium. Hagerty says tan or sand interiors and blue, green or white paint sell best.

buying_checks.head: Ask where it lived
buying_checks.body: Kerr won't buy trucks from road-salt states and estimates about 20% of needed parts have to come from salvage yards. A dry-state truck with a known history is worth paying for.

repairs.title: Rebuild the Motorcraft 2150 or convert to throttle-body injection
repairs.cost: TBI conversion about $2,000 in parts plus up to $1,000 labor (Hagerty)
repairs.symptoms: Hesitation, stumbling or stalling cold or hot, hard hot starts, fuel smell, poor idle. Hagerty's specialist blames the carburetor for about 40% of owner headaches.
repairs.fix: Rule out vacuum leaks and ignition faults first: check every vacuum line and the distributor pickup and module. To rebuild, remove the carb, strip it on a clean bench, replace the base gasket, power valve and internal gaskets from a 2150 kit, set the float and choke pull-off to the kit's specs, and refit on a new base gasket and insulator. Converting to TBI means a throttle body with its own fuel pump, return line, sensors and harness. Most owners who keep the truck do it eventually, and it's the core of the Wagonmaster recipe.
repairs.tools: Carb rebuild kit with specs · gasket scraper · carb cleaner · vacuum gauge · timing light · for TBI: fuel-line tools, wiring tools, laptop or handheld tuner per kit

parts.name: Carburetor overhaul kit for Motorcraft 2150, V8 1981–1991

repairs.title: Replace the rear main seal (AMC 360)
repairs.symptoms: Oil dripping from where the engine meets the transmission, with no obvious leak above it. Hagerty lists rear main leaks as a common 360 fault.
repairs.fix: Rule out the valve covers, intake and oil-pressure sender first, because oil runs downhill to the bellhousing. Then drain the oil, support the engine, and drop the oil pan; on a full-size Jeep, front axle and crossmember clearance make this the hard part. Remove the rear main cap, pull both seal halves, clean the grooves, install the new seal, refit the cap to the factory torque spec, and refit the pan with a new gasket. Fill and check for leaks after a heat cycle.
repairs.tools: Floor jack and stands · engine support · torque wrench · seal pick · RTV per seal instructions · factory service manual for torque specs [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]

parts.name: Rear main crankshaft oil seal, V8-360/401 1974–1991

repairs.title: Fix a dead power window (flex rack and motor)
repairs.symptoms: You can hear the motor run, but the glass doesn't move or moves in jerks. Hagerty says window flex tracks snap often on these trucks.
repairs.fix: Remove the door panel carefully, since water-damaged panels are common and the clips break. Peel back the vapor barrier and support the glass. Unbolt the motor and regulator assembly and inspect the plastic flex rack, which is the usual failure. Fit a new rack, lube the channel, fit new mounting grommets and screws, and check the motor's pigtail connector for corrosion before refitting the panel.
repairs.tools: Door-panel clip tool · glass holder · screwdrivers and sockets · white lithium grease

parts.name: Power window flex rack gear replacement, 1981–1991
Power window motor mounting screw set, 1980–1991
Window motor weather-tight pigtail and connector set, 1984–1991

repairs.title: Revive the tailgate window
repairs.symptoms: The rear glass won't go down, so the interior tailgate handle can't be reached. YourMechanic says the tailgate window is 'notorious for failing'.
repairs.fix: Test the dash switch and the key switch in the tailgate first; Hagerty says the rear switch often dies. If the motor hums but the glass doesn't move, open the tailgate inner panel (lower the glass by hand with the manual crank if you need to) and check the lifter cushions and glass channels for binding. Replace worn cushions and channels, lube the tracks, and fit a new switch if needed.
repairs.tools: Trim tools · test light or multimeter · sockets · silicone or lithium lube

parts.name: Tailgate window dash switch with harness, 1986–1991

repairs.title: Patch floors, rockers and lower quarters
repairs.symptoms: Wet or crunchy carpet, holes under the driver's floor mat, bubbling under the woodgrain, rotten rockers that can let exhaust into the cabin.
repairs.fix: Pull the seats and carpet and wire-brush everything so you can see the full extent. Cut out rot back to clean metal, then trial-fit and weld in repair sections: front driver's and passenger's floor, rear sections, rockers, dog legs and lower quarters. Seam-seal and undercoat. On the outside, remove the woodgrain before welding and put down fresh vinyl afterward.
repairs.tools: MIG welder · cut-off wheel · spot-weld drill · clamps · weld-through primer · seam sealer

repairs.title: Drop the fuel tank and replace the skid plate and straps
repairs.symptoms: Rust where the tank meets the body, a sagging or perforated skid plate, fuel smell, a sending unit that reads wrong. Both Hagerty and YourMechanic name this area.
repairs.fix: Run the tank nearly empty and disconnect the battery. Support the skid plate and tank with a jack, remove the skid-plate bolts and straps, disconnect the filler and vent hoses and the sender wiring, and lower the assembly. Inspect the frame and body above it. Treat the rust, then refit with a new skid plate (or the master kit), insulator mat, straps and fresh hardware.
repairs.tools: Transmission jack or floor jack with board · penetrating oil · fuel-line clamps · sockets

parts.name: Fuel tank skid plate master kit, 1980–1991
Fuel tank skid plate rubber insulator mat, 1980–1991

repairs.title: Selec-Trac won't engage: vacuum system and transfer-case service
repairs.symptoms: The dash 2WD/4WD control does nothing, the truck stays in one mode, or 4WD drops out. Hagerty says to check that 4WD engages on the fly; seals leak with age.
repairs.fix: Selec-Trac uses vacuum to shift between 2WD and 4WD. Check the vacuum lines from the engine to the reservoir, the dash switch and the transfer-case actuator for cracks or disconnected hoses, and test with a hand vacuum pump. On 1984–86 trucks, the transfer-case vacuum switch is a known replacement part. Fix any seal leaks at the yokes, then drain and refill the transfer case (Team Grand Wagoneer recommends a synthetic ATF-type fluid).
repairs.tools: Hand vacuum pump · vacuum hose · sockets · drain pan · fluid pump

parts.name: Vacuum reservoir tank with mounting screws, 1974–1991

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: We couldn't find a forum consensus we trust for the SJ, so we won't guess. The factory size is P235/75R15 on 15x7 six-lug alloys (1989 spec). Anything larger should be test-fitted at full lock and with the suspension compressed. Team Grand Wagoneer sells a 3-inch lift kit with springs and shocks for owners who want more. Running bigger tires on yours? Tell us through Show Us Your Rig.

faq.q: How much power does the 360 V8 make?
faq.a: It depends on the source. Hagerty quotes 140 hp and 280 lb-ft, Offroaders.com says 144 hp, and Wikipedia's AMC V8 entry lists 160 hp for the two-barrel 360 from 1978 to 1991. Either way, the torque is what moves it. The 360 is a tall-deck AMC engine. Chrysler kept building it until 1991, changing only the casting from '360' to '5.9L'.

faq.q: What fuel economy should I expect?
faq.a: Not much. Wikipedia cites a combined 11 mpg, and Hagerty says single digits in town and about a dozen on the highway with the V8. Fuel prices after the 1990 oil shock helped kill the truck. TBI conversions are said to help, but don't expect miracles from a carbureted-era V8 in a 4,000-plus-pound wagon.
Jeep's 1989 spec lists 5,000 lb maximum trailer weight (750 lb tongue) with the Class III Package B, and 3,500 lb (350 lb tongue) with the Class I and II Package A.

Most are Selec-Trac: an NP228 or NP229 (the 229 adds a viscous coupling) with a dash control that shifts between 2WD and 4WD on the move using vacuum. Offroaders.com says some 1984–88 Grand Wagoneers used the part-time NP208 instead. Going between 4-High and 4-Low takes neutral and a crawl of under 5 mph.

1989–91, if you can. Those years got better rust-proofing (electrocoat primer), base-clear paint, an improved A/C compressor, an overhead console, keyless entry and a rear wiper. The 1991 Final Edition carries a premium. Hagerty's specialist adds that low mileage, under about 100,000, is the safest buy.

Every Grand Wagoneer left the factory with a carburetor, a two-barrel Motorcraft on the 360. Throttle-body injection kits are the most common upgrade. Hagerty puts the conversion at about $2,000 in parts and up to $1,000 in labor, and Wagonmaster builds its trucks around a Howell TBI system.

Values rose for years. In one report, Hagerty listed a 1991 at $36,900 in #2 condition and $62,200 in #1, and said a nice #3 driver shouldn't cost much more than $20,000. Restomods from Wagonmaster or Classic Gentleman were $40,000–80,000 in 2019. These figures are dated, so check current Hagerty valuations and recent BaT results.

faq.q: Is this the same as the Wagoneer Limited (XJ)?
faq.a: No. From 1984 to 1990 Jeep also sold a compact, unibody Wagoneer based on the [[jeep/cherokee-xj|Cherokee XJ]], with woodgrain decals. The Grand Wagoneer is the full-size, body-on-frame SJ.

Mostly. Specialists such as Team Grand Wagoneer and BJ's Off Road stock everything from floor pans to woodgrain vinyl. But Hagerty's specialist estimates about 20% of the parts a restoration needs come from salvage yards, and front fenders are no longer available.

Yes. It's vinyl, not wood. The 1987–91 trucks use 'marine teak' and earlier trucks the cherry-oak style, and replacement kits are sold for both. Fix any rust under the old vinyl first, because bubbles usually mean the metal is rotting.
